extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (elementary/secondary/postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, institutional administrators, investigators, decision-makers, and Title IX counsel
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX grievance and reporting standards
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements from the Department of Education's Title IX final regulations governing notice/actual knowledge, reporting mechanisms, Title IX Coordinator duties, supportive measures, grievance processes (formal and informal), evidence handling, training, and distinctions between elementary/secondary and postsecondary institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evidence obtained from law enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations precludes a recipient from using evidence obtained from law enforcement in a §106.45 grievance process, subject to requirements in §106.45 such as that evidence sent to the parties for inspection and review must be directly related to the allegations under investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence gathered by law enforcement may be included if directly related to the allegations; recipients must still comply with §106.45 obligations (e.g., inspection/review rules). The preamble notes legal standards for criminal investigations differ and police reports may not be determinative for Title IX purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of all relevant evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A grievance process must provide for objective evaluation of all relevant evidence, inculpatory and exculpatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure investigators/decision-makers consider and evaluate both inculpatory and exculpatory evidence. This is a statutory/regulatory requirement under §106.45 and is emphasized as a guardrail against biased processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence disclosure limited to material directly related to allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence sent to the parties for inspection and review must be directly related to the allegations under investigation (§106.45(b)(5)(vi)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sharing evidence with parties, recipients must limit disclosure to material directly related to the reported allegations; this constraint applies even when using outside-source evidence (e.g., law enforcement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution — voluntary written consent and substantive exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(b)(9) allows informal resolution processes only with the written, voluntary consent of both parties, with notice to the parties about ramifications; informal resolution may not be offered for allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may offer mediation/other informal options when both parties knowingly and voluntarily agree in writing and after receiving notice of ramifications; do not offer informal resolution for employee-on-student sexual harassment allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures defined and required
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.30 defines 'supportive measures' as individualized services, reasonably available, offered without fee or charge, designed to restore or preserve a complainant's equal access to the recipient's education program or activity without unreasonably burdening the other party, and/or designed to protect the complainant's safety or deter sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX Coordinators are responsible for effective implementation of supportive measures (§106.30 and §106.45(b)(7)(iv)). Supportive measures must be available with or without filing a formal complaint and cannot impose unreasonable burden on the other party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity for advisors and access to supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer both parties the same opportunity to select an advisor of the party's choice and must offer supportive measures to complainants (§106.45(b)(5)(iv); §106.44(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance processes must treat parties equitably by providing equal advisor-selection opportunities and by offering supportive measures regardless of filing a formal complaint; Title IX Coordinator must contact complainants to discuss these options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of non-responsibility during grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: A presumption of non-responsibility applies to respondents during the grievance process; it does not permit automatically or prematurely 'believ[ing] respondents' or 'disbeliev[ing] complainants.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must maintain procedural fairness; presumption of non-responsibility means the respondent is presumed not responsible until a determination is reached, but this does not justify bias for or against either party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions in §106.30 apply across Part 106 (with limited exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department revised the NPRM position and now states the definitions in §106.30 should apply to Part 106 of Title 34 of the CFR, except for the definitions of the words 'elementary and secondary school' and 'postsecondary institution,' which will apply only to §§106.44 and 106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change is framed as non-substantive clarification to ensure clarity and consistency; §106.81 clarifies §106.30 definitions do not apply to certain Title VI procedural provisions incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any person may report and accessible reporting methods
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.8(a): 'Any person may report sex discrimination, including sexual harassment... in person, by mail, by telephone, or by electronic mail... or by any other means that results in the Title IX Coordinator receiving the person's verbal or written report.' A report may be made at any time, including during non-business hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure reporting mechanisms (office address, telephone, email) for the Title IX Coordinator are available and that reports can be made via multiple means and at any time; reporting may come from victims or third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator identification and contact information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must designate and 'authorize' a Title IX Coordinator and must notify students and employees of the Title IX Coordinator's contact information, which must include office address, telephone number, and email; contact information must be prominently displayed on recipients' websites (§106.8(a); §106.8(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must use the title 'Title IX Coordinator' in notices and make contact info easy to find; for accessibility, include day-or-night options (email/phone) and ensure multiple ways to contact the Coordinator are prominently posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge standard — K-12 vs postsecondary distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.30 defines 'actual knowledge' to include notice to any elementary and secondary school employee, or to any Title IX Coordinator; for postsecondary institutions, actual knowledge requires notice to a Title IX Coordinator or an official with authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K-12 recipients are charged with actual knowledge when any employee has notice (to ensure prompt response for minors). Postsecondary institutions may limit mandatory-reporting designations to some employees, preserving certain confidentiality options for students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and reporting obligations do not automatically create 'official with authority'
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere fact that an individual is required to, or has been trained to, report sexual harassment does not mean that individual is an 'official with authority.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may train or require reporting from contractors, volunteers, or others without converting them into officials whose knowledge triggers actual knowledge for the institution. This prevents training policies from unintentionally increasing institutional liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator may sign a formal complaint in limited circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator may, when it is not clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances, sign a formal complaint that initiates a §106.45 grievance process even when that is not what the complainant wished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinators have the authority to file when circumstances justify it, but should weigh complainant autonomy and known circumstances to avoid initiating grievance processes contrary to a complainant's wishes absent reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory training and impartiality requirements for Title IX personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations require training for Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and any person who facilitates an informal resolution process; Title IX Coordinators must be free from conflicts of interest and bias (§106.45(b)(1)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must include how to serve impartially and avoid bias; institutions should ensure personnel charged with Title IX roles receive appropriate, documented training to satisfy regulatory requirements and reduce risk of procedural unfairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' equitable response obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must respond equitably by offering supportive measures to a complainant and by refraining from taking disciplinary action against a respondent without first following a grievance process that complies with §106.45 (§106.44(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional responses must balance support for complainants with procedural protections for respondents; disciplinary action should follow a compliant grievance process, and supportive measures should be provided promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of reporting options and information to avoid 'falling through the cracks'
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations require each postsecondary institution to inform students and employees about how to report to the Title IX Coordinator and that every institution has accessible options for any person to report (e.g., email or phone, prominently displayed on websites) that can be used day or night (§106.8; §106.30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should prominently display multiple reporting options, ensure third parties can report, and make the Title IX Coordinator accessible to reduce situations where reports are not acted upon or are 'swept under the rug.'

rubrics_metrics.name: No universal mandatory reporting requirement for postsecondary institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department does not require universal/near-universal mandatory reporting by postsecondary institutions; institutions may choose which employees must report sexual harassment and which may be confidential resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postsecondary institutions may design their own mandatory-reporting policies, balancing benefits of broad reporting against harms (e.g., chilling disclosures); however, this flexibility is coupled with strong requirements that institutions inform the community how to report to the Title IX Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant autonomy regarding filing formal complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant always retains the option of initiating a grievance process by filing a formal complaint and is never required to file a formal complaint in order to receive supportive measures (§106.44(a); §106.30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX Coordinators must discuss supportive measures and the option to file a formal complaint with complainants; offering supportive measures does not compel a complainant to file, though Coordinators may sign complaints in limited circumstances (see related criterion).
